newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end lower but Clariant soars.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end lower but Clariant soars.

text.p: Swiss shares ended lower but above the day's lows while chemicals group Clariant surged more than 12 percent, extending yesterday's strong gain.
U.S. PPI data sent mixed signals and did not influence prices much, dealers said. Swiss indices moved off the day's low after Wall Street's early losses proved only moderate.
Clariant shot up 64 Swiss francs to 572, continuing Tuesday's bull run after saying it would acquire the speciality chemicals business of Germany's Hoechst in a merger.
The blue-chip SMI index down 27.8 points, or 0.72 percent, at 3,857.6. SMI's low for the day was 3,817.3 points.
All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended down 16.89 points, or 0.68 percent, at 2,464.85.

"At the moment, negative news has an immediate impact on prices", a dealer said. He cited fears of a correction on financial markets and concern that U.S. interest rate may be raised and Japanese investors may pull out of the U.S. market.
"Everyone takes profits where they can", a trader said.
Among financials, CS Holding and insurer Zurich closed flat at 134 francs and 365 francs, respectively.
Baloise fell more than three percent to 2,855 francs, giving up some recent gains.
Roche certificates gave up 110 francs to stand at 9,970. Ciba and Sandoz also yielded around one percent each.
Second-tier Esec plummeted eight 8.6 percent to 4,800 francs after a downgrade, dealers said.
